samuel2.18.p1.b1.text: Then David reviewed his troops and appointed over them commanders of hundreds and of thousands.

samuel2.18.p1.b2.text: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite.

samuel2.18.p1.b3.text: “I will surely march out with you as well.”

samuel2.18.p1.b4.text: “You must not go out! … but you are worth ten thousand of us. It is better for now if you support us from the city.”

samuel2.18.p2.b1.text: “I will do whatever seems best to you”

samuel2.18.p2.b2.text: So he stood beside the gate, while all the troops marched out by hundreds and by thousands.

samuel2.18.p2.b3.text: “Treat the young man Absalom gently for my sake.”

samuel2.18.p2.b4.text: And all the people heard the king’s orders to each of the commanders regarding Absalom.

samuel2.18.p3.b1.text: So David’s army marched into the field to engage Israel in the battle, which took place in the forest of Ephraim.

samuel2.18.p3.b2.text: There the people of Israel were defeated by David’s servants, and the slaughter was great that day—twenty thousand men.

samuel2.18.p3.b3.text: … that day the forest devoured more people than the sword.

samuel2.18.p4.b1.text: Now Absalom was riding on his mule when he met the servants of David,

samuel2.18.p4.b2.text: … as the mule went under the thick branches of a large oak, Absalom’s head was caught fast in the tree.

samuel2.18.p4.b3.text: The mule under him kept going, so that he was suspended in midair.

samuel2.18.p5.b1.text: “I just saw Absalom hanging in an oak tree!”

samuel2.18.p5.b2.text: “You just saw him! … Why did you not strike him to the ground right there? I would have given you ten shekels of silver and a warrior’s belt!”

samuel2.18.p5.b3.text: “Even if a thousand shekels of silver were weighed out into my hands, I would not raise my hand against the son of the king.”

samuel2.18.p5.b4.text: “For we heard the king command you and Abishai and Ittai, ‘Protect the young man Absalom for my sake.’”

samuel2.18.p6.b1.text: “I am not going to wait like this with you!”

samuel2.18.p6.b2.text: And he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the oak tree.

samuel2.18.p6.b3.text: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.

samuel2.18.p7.b1.text: Then Joab blew the ram’s horn, and the troops broke off their pursuit of Israel because Joab had restrained them.

samuel2.18.p7.b2.text: They took Absalom, cast him into a large pit in the forest, and piled a huge mound of stones over him.

samuel2.18.p7.b3.text: “I have no son to preserve the memory of my name.”

samuel2.18.p7.b4.text: So he gave the pillar his name, and to this day it is called Absalom’s Monument.

samuel2.18.p8.b1.text: “Please let me run and tell the king the good news that the LORD has avenged him of his enemies.”

samuel2.18.p8.b2.text: “You are not the man to take good news today. … because the king’s son is dead.”

samuel2.18.p8.b3.text: “No matter what, I want to run!”

samuel2.18.p8.b4.text: So Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.

samuel2.18.p9.b1.text: Now David was sitting between the two gates when the watchman went up to the roof of the gateway by the wall, looked out, and saw a man running alone.

samuel2.18.p9.b3.text: “The first man appears to me to be running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok.”

samuel2.18.p9.b4.text: “This is a good man … He comes with good news.”

samuel2.18.p10.b2.text: “Is the young man Absalom all right?”

samuel2.18.p10.b3.text: “… I saw a great tumult, but I do not know what it was.”

samuel2.18.p10.b4.text: “May what has become of the young man happen to the enemies of my lord the king and to all who rise up against you to harm you.”

samuel2.18.p11.b1.text: The king was shaken and went up to the gate chamber and wept. And as he walked, he cried out,

samuel2.18.p11.b2.text: “O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!”

samuel2.18.p11.b3.text: “If only I had died instead of you, O Absalom, my son, my son!”
